claim: On 2 tasks in the corpus, claude-opus-4-7 reached a strictly higher medal tier than claude-sonnet-4-6 (leaf-classification: silver vs bronze; spooky-author-identification: bronze vs none).

task_b.name: spooky-author-identification
task_b.delta: +1 medal tier @ +$45 (but 'none' on sonnet may indicate transient failure rather than capability gap)

scope: These two tasks both involve nuanced discrimination — fine-grained leaf species classification and author-identification stylometry. Unclear whether 'opus bridges tier' is a property of (a) the task family, (b) a specific role (likely coder or tuner), or (c) noise from n=1.
limitations: n=1 per (task, model) for these comparisons. Could easily be variance — a re-run of sonnet on leaf-classification might also get silver.

We do not know WHICH role is responsible for the tier difference. Possible the difference comes from sonnet-tuner running out of attempts, or sonnet-coder writing a slightly weaker train.py. Without per-role-mixed runs we cannot localize.
spooky 'none' may not be a model-capability failure; it may be the same rate-limit / process-kill class of issue we have already observed in other corners of the corpus.
